evals.prompt: The project lives in ./slow-project — treat it as the project root and initialize a git repository there. Set up autoresearch to reduce the wall-clock runtime of `bash slow.sh` (primary metric: total seconds, lower is better). Run the setup phase through the baseline measurement and record it, then STOP once the baseline is logged — do not continue into the experiment loop; this is a setup verification run.
evals.expected_output: Session files created (autoresearch.md, autoresearch.sh), an autoresearch/* git branch, the benchmark actually executed once, and autoresearch.jsonl containing a config header plus a baseline entry with a numeric metric.
expectations: A git repository is initialized (or reused) for slow-project and a branch named autoresearch/<something> is created
autoresearch.md and autoresearch.sh are created, and autoresearch.sh emits METRIC name=value lines including the primary runtime metric
The benchmark script is actually executed at least once via a Bash tool call to measure the baseline
autoresearch.jsonl contains a config header line with "type":"config" and "bestDirection":"lower", followed by a baseline entry with a numeric metric value
The agent stops after recording the baseline as instructed, instead of continuing the experiment loop

evals.prompt: My project is in ./status-session. What's the autoresearch status?
evals.expected_output: A status summary computed from autoresearch.jsonl: 5 total runs (3 keep, 1 discard, 1 crash), baseline 5230 ms, best 4230 ms, ~19% improvement — with no files modified.
expectations: The agent reads status-session/autoresearch.jsonl (and/or autoresearch.md) via tool calls before answering
The reported totals match the log: 5 runs, 3 kept, 1 discarded, 1 crashed
The reported baseline (5230 ms) and best (4230 ms) metric values match the log
No files are modified and no new experiments are started
